Title: Amjschmitz
Review_Text: I’m not sure what the actual boundaries are of the gothic quarter, and maybe they aren’t rigidly defined. But you’ll know it if you’re in it because much of the architecture will have that medieval feel to it. There are statues and basilicas and so many cool, narrow alleys. Be aware that it is a popular area for tourists, so it will always be crowded. And because the streets are narrow that could lead to some frustration. We went in January so it wasn’t too bad but I can imagine a more popular month being a little harder to get around. Expect a lot of graffiti. Like Rome, it seems to be everywhere. But most of it seems to be more of the artistic variety as opposed to gang markings. Every single roll down metal store front is a canvas (not just in this quarter, but throughout Barcelona) to the point that I wonder if many of these are commissioned.

Title: Kristen T
Review_Text: I debated about giving this 3 or 4 circles and decided on four. Seeing Gaudi's work was a main draw for me in visiting Barcelona. I had seen countless pictures of his work, including the Park, during my research phase and wanted to see it all in person. Getting to the Park was not as easy as getting to other major sites in Barcelona. We took the metro to the Park Guell stop, but then had to walk about 10-15 minutes (some uphill a bit) to reach the park entrance. Luckily we were able to enter even though we arrived past our pre-purchased ticket window time. The park has a nice walking path, but the main highlights, especially with the mosaic tile benches, are overrun with people. Plus the pictures I had seen prior to visiting made it seem like it would be a lot more colorful than it ended up being. Dang photo editing making it look better than in person! There were a lot of people just hanging out on the benches blocking photo opportunities. It was kind of frustrating, but then you remember they are benches and made for sitting... We went into one of the buildings which had some signs, pictures and videos about the park project and how it ended up being what it is today. Visiting that first might be smart to have a better understanding of the park as a whole. Looking back, I'm glad we went but I wouldn't recommend putting this at the top of your must-see list while in Barcelona.

It also summarizes everything about Barcelona...great place, picturesque, fun...but watch out for pickpockets. I guarantee mre than half of the reviews here will say to watch out for pickpockets. Title: Amjschmitz
Review_Text: I’m not sure what the actual boundaries are of the gothic quarter, and maybe they aren’t rigidly defined. But you’ll know it if you’re in it because much of the architecture will have that medieval feel to it. There are statues and basilicas and so many cool, narrow alleys. Be aware that it is a popular area for tourists, so it will always be crowded. And because the streets are narrow that could lead to some frustration. We went in January so it wasn’t too bad but I can imagine a more popular month being a little harder to get around. Expect a lot of graffiti. Like Rome, it seems to be everywhere. But most of it seems to be more of the artistic variety as opposed to gang markings. Every single roll down metal store front is a canvas (not just in this quarter, but throughout Barcelona) to the point that I wonder if many of these are commissioned.
